ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an inverting operational amplifier circuit. The AC input source is connected to a 10 kΩ resistor, and the other end of the resistor is connected to the inverting input terminal (−) of the op-amp. The non-inverting input terminal (+) of the op-amp is grounded. The output terminal is fed back to the inverting input terminal through a 30 kΩ resistor. The Ri marked in the figure is the input resistance looking into the amplifier to the right from the input-source terminal. Reasoning: When an ideal op-amp operates under negative feedback, because the non-inverting terminal is grounded, the inverting terminal is a virtual ground, and the voltage is approximately 0 V; at the same time, the input terminal of the ideal op-amp does not absorb current. Therefore the current seen by the input source only flows through the series 10 kΩ input resistor, and the feedback resistor is not directly the resistance seen from the input terminal. Therefore the input resistance Ri = 10 kΩ.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is an inverting operational-amplifier circuit with the + input grounded, a 10 kΩ resistor from the source/input terminal to the − input, and a 30 kΩ feedback resistor from output to the − input. Then apply the ideal op-amp virtual-ground rule: because the + input is at ground and feedback is present, the − input node is approximately 0 V and no current enters the op-amp input. Thus, from the source side, the only resistance encountered is the 10 kΩ input resistor, so Ri = 10 kΩ.
